title: Is Carpet Outdated in 2026? Where It Still Wins
meta: Carpet is not outdated in 2026, it moved upstairs. Wills Flooring explains where carpet still beats hard floors in Kirkland homes and where it hurts resale.
keywords: is carpet outdated 2026, carpet vs hardwood bedrooms, is carpet coming back, wall to wall carpet 2026, carpet in bedrooms Kirkland

blocks.lead: Carpet is not outdated in 2026, but wall-to-wall carpet on a main floor is. It has moved upstairs, into bedrooms, bonus rooms, stairs and media rooms, where it still beats every hard floor on comfort, sound and warmth.
blocks.detail: Buyers in Kirkland expect hardwood or vinyl plank in living rooms, kitchens and hallways. The same buyers walk into a carpeted bedroom and feel relieved. Carpet is also the cheapest floor we install, $0.99 per sq ft in labor against $2.50 for vinyl plank and $3.25 for hardwood, so the question is not whether carpet is dated, it is which rooms it belongs in.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks whether carpet makes a house look like a 1990s rental. The honest answer from a company that installs both carpet and hardwood every week: it depends on the room. We pull carpet out of Houghton and Rose Hill living rooms most months and put hardwood or vinyl plank down. We also lay new carpet upstairs in those same houses, on the same job.

blocks.text: Why people think carpet is outdated

items.title: Open-plan main floors
items.text: Kitchens now flow into living rooms, and nobody wants a carpet edge six feet from a stove. Once the kitchen is hard floor the living room follows. That is why carpet left the main floor, not fashion.

items.title: Listing photos
items.text: Hardwood photographs well. Beige carpet photographs like beige carpet. Kirkland listings compete on photos, so sellers rip out main-floor carpet before listing and buyers learn to expect it.

items.title: Pets and allergies
items.text: Older cut pile held pet hair and dust. Low-pile nylon and triexta release it far better, but the reputation stuck, and vinyl plank arrived in time to take the pet-owner market.

items.title: Builder-grade memories
items.text: What people remember as dated is thin polyester on a cheap pad, flat in the traffic lane after five years. Good carpet on a dense pad does not look like that at year ten.

blocks.text: What carpet does that hard floors cannot

items.html: Sound. A carpeted upstairs over a hardwood main floor is the quietest layout there is. Vinyl plank on the best underlayment still transmits footfall that carpet on a pad absorbs. Anyone in a Totem Lake condo with a neighbor below knows it.

Warmth. Carpet and pad add real insulation over a crawlspace or a garage. In Bridle Trails, where 1970s and 1980s homes put bedrooms over unheated garages, that is the difference between socks and no socks.
Falls. Stairs and toddlers, stairs and dogs, stairs and anyone over seventy. Carpet forgives what hardwood punishes.
Speed, disruption and cost. A whole upstairs is carpeted in one day, with no sanding and no cure time, at the lowest labor rate on our price list.

Easy resets. Replacing bedroom carpet before a sale is a one-day job at $0.99 per sq ft plus $0.45 to take the old carpet away. Refinishing a scratched hardwood bedroom is neither as quick nor as cheap.

blocks.html: Money is part of why carpet stayed upstairs. Our labor for stretch-in carpet is $0.99 per sq ft with $30 per step, against $2.50 per sq ft and $100 per stair for vinyl plank and $3.25 per sq ft and $125 per stair for hardwood. A 900 sq ft Juanita upstairs with 14 stairs is 900 × $0.99 + 14 × $30 = $891 + $420 = $1,311 in carpet labor. The same floor in vinyl plank is 900 × $2.50 + 14 × $100 = $2,250 + $1,400 = $3,650. Carpet and pad are quoted on top of that at the estimate, and so is the plank, but the gap does not close.

blocks.text: When carpet is the wrong call, honestly

items.title: Main floor of a house you are selling
items.text: If the living room is carpeted and the kitchen is not, Kirkland buyers price a floor replacement into their offer. Hardwood or vinyl plank on the main level pays for itself in most Eastside listings. Upstairs does not need to change.

items.title: Any room with a water source
items.text: Kitchens, bathrooms, laundry rooms and mudrooms. A wet pad grows mold under a carpet that looks fine on top. Vinyl plank belongs here. See our guide to which rooms should have carpet.

items.title: Dogs with accidents
items.text: A puppy or a senior dog will defeat any carpet eventually. Use it in the rooms the dog does not sleep in, and put a waterproof pad under any carpet it does.

items.title: Below-grade rooms without a moisture plan
items.text: A Kirkland daylight basement can be carpeted, but only after a moisture test and with a pad that does not absorb water. Skipping that is why basement carpet has its reputation.

blocks.title: The mistake we see most:
blocks.text: Homeowners replace good bedroom carpet with vinyl plank because they read that carpet is dated, then live with cold floors and echo upstairs. If the carpet is under eight years old and not worn, keep it and put the money into the main floor, where a hard floor earns it back.
How to choose carpet that will not look dated in 2036

items.html: Pick a mid-tone neutral, not a trend color. Warm gray and oatmeal have been safe for a decade. Anything named after a food or a jewel will date.
Go lower and denser, not taller. Fold the sample back. If you see the backing easily, it will mat in the hallway.
Match the pad to the room. Firm and dense for stairs and halls, a little softer in bedrooms, moisture-barrier where pets sleep.
Stop carpet at the bedroom door, not the hallway. A hard-floor upstairs hall with carpeted bedrooms reads current. Carpet flowing down the hall reads 2004.
Look at samples in your own light. Bedrooms facing the lake get very different light from Rose Hill rooms facing the trees. We bring samples to the house for exactly that reason.
Get the whole plan in one quote. The best houses we work on do carpet upstairs and hardwood or vinyl plank downstairs on one visit, with matching transitions. Ask for both at the same free estimate.

faq.q: Do buyers in Kirkland still accept carpet in bedrooms?
faq.a: Yes. Almost every Kirkland listing we prepare keeps or replaces bedroom carpet rather than converting to hard floors. Agents ask for main-floor hardwood or vinyl plank and fresh, neutral carpet upstairs. Buyers with young kids often prefer it.

faq.q: Is carpet coming back in style?
faq.a: In specific rooms, yes. Bedrooms, bonus rooms and media rooms are moving back toward carpet after a decade of hard floors everywhere, mainly because of noise and cold. Patterned and textured loops are also more popular than they have been since the 1990s.

Carpet on a main floor next to a hard-floor kitchen usually costs you at sale, because buyers assume they will replace it. Carpet in bedrooms and bonus rooms does not lower value if it is clean and neutral. Worn or stained carpet anywhere costs you more than replacing it.

faq.q: What carpet colors look current in 2026?
faq.a: Warm grays, greige, oatmeal, mushroom and soft taupe. Cooler grays are fading. Patterns are small and tone-on-tone rather than bold. Anything with a strong color cast, including the beige-pink of older builder carpet, reads dated.

faq.q: How long does modern carpet last?
faq.a: Eight to fifteen years depending on fiber, density and pad. Nylon and triexta on a dense pad in bedrooms can pass fifteen. Polyester in a hallway may look tired at six. The pad matters as much as the carpet.

faq.q: Should I carpet stairs in a house with hardwood downstairs?
faq.a: It is the most common Kirkland setup we install: hardwood main floor, carpeted stairs and bedrooms. Stairs are $30 per step in labor, so a 14-tread flight is $420 plus the carpet. A runner over hardwood treads is the other option, and either is safer and quieter than bare wood.
